## Simulated data
Every output on this page comes from the package's simulated data. It shows what this step produces and how to read it. It says nothing about any real state: every gap, ratio and rate here comes from how the data were generated.
:::

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(stateELP)
```

Check 3 sets English learners' (ELs') content-test scores beside their
English language proficiency (ELP), grade by grade, with former ELs and
never-EL students as reference groups.

## What this step answers

**At what level of English proficiency does language stop being the main
thing holding back performance on the content test? And is the bar the state
sets one that English-only peers clear themselves?**

The state's *proficiency cut* is the lowest scale score of the academic level
the state calls proficient. If at least half the students in an ELP band
reach it, students at that level of English perform on the content test the
way the state expects of anyone. If they do not, the content test may still
be measuring their English along with their subject knowledge.

That level is then set against the exit threshold. Students who exit below it
leave while the content test is still partly a language test for them. A
threshold well above it holds students longer than the state's own content
standard requires.

The step answers this three ways for each grade and subject: **box plots** of
scores by ELP band; a **logistic regression** of the chance of reaching the
cut, read at the ELP score where that chance is 50%; and **landing
statistics** that put the grades side by side. Two **fairness checks** then
ask whether English-only peers clear the same bar.

## Sample

**Cross-sectional: every current EL in one grade who has a score on one
content test in one school year, plus former ELs and English-only students in
the same grade, subject and year.**

Checks 1 and 2 follow one entry cohort (students who entered EL status in the
same grade and year) forward through time. Check 3 takes a one-year snapshot
instead. It includes every EL in the grade, whenever they entered, so recent
arrivals sit beside students in their sixth year of status.

- **A student is in the sample because they sat the content test.** The
  package starts from the academic table and attaches roster status to it.
  Starting from the roster or the ELP table would drop the reference groups.
  An untested student is outside this sample, not missing from it.
- **Each grade and subject is its own *panel*. Grades are never pooled.** The
  simulated spec declares ELA and Math in grades 3 through 11. Each panel
  uses the most recent year with academic scores.
- **The groups** are current ELs split into ELP bands (the spec's grouping of
  the reported proficiency level), current ELs with no annual ELP score that
  year, former ELs, and English-only students (`EL_STATUS == "never"`). A
  former EL is never counted as English-only.
- **In the simulated data**, former ELs leave the data four years after
  exiting, so "Former ELs" means former within four years. English-only
  students are a 10% sample with a `SAMPLE_WEIGHT` of 10.
- **The logistic regression uses current ELs only.** No one else has an ELP
  score to regress on.

## Status in the package

**Built.** Every output slot the stage's instruction file lists is filled,
including the check for multi-criterion rules. The stage's tests have no
skips, and its report renders to Word and HTML. Four things are not built:

- **A matched English-only group.** Fairness check (a) *filters* on one
  free-or-reduced-price lunch flag (`FRL`). Matching is a recorded later
  addition.
- **A year dimension.** Each panel takes the most recent year only.
- **A display of the multi-criterion check** in the stage report. Read it
  from the results object (last section).
- **A "screened but not classified" group.** The instruction file describes
  it as a spec-gated column (empty for the simulated data). No slot or
  column exists for it yet.

## Before you start

You need an `el_spec` and an `el_data` bundle that includes the academic
table. Check 3 reads these parts of the spec:

| Spec field | What Check 3 uses it for |
|---|---|
| `academic$<subject>$grades` | Which grades get a panel. A subject with `grades = NULL` (an end-of-course test) takes its grades from the data. |
| `academic$<subject>$cuts` and `policy$academic_benchmark$proficient_level` | The proficiency cut: the red line, the share at or above it, and the logistic outcome. |
| `elp$bands` | The band columns and their order. |
| `elp$administration_window` | The note on how the two tests are paired in time. |
| `policy$exit` | The band the exit threshold falls in, and the rule's Type. |
| `policy$suppression$min_cell` | The smallest group whose statistics are shown. |

```{r}
spec <- read_el_spec("00_SIM_EL_Spec")

spec_academic_subjects(spec)
spec_academic_grades(spec, "ELA")
spec$academic$ELA$cuts                        # minimum score of levels 2 to 5
spec$policy$academic_benchmark$proficient_level
spec_headline_label(spec)                     # the ELP score the exit rule uses
spec$elp$administration_window
spec_min_cell(spec)
```

Here the cut is level 4's minimum,
`r spec$academic$ELA$cuts[[spec$policy$academic_benchmark$proficient_level - 1]]`.
The simulated cuts carry `source = "provisional"`, the spec's form of
`[DERIVED — VERIFY]`. For a real state, take them from an official table.

Build the bundle once and reuse it:

```{r}
bundle <- as_el_data(el_long_sim,
                     roster   = el_roster_sim,
                     academic = academic_long_sim,
                     spec     = spec)
nrow(el_academic(bundle))
```

A missing input never stops the stage. The affected slots come back `NULL` or
empty:

| Missing input | What happens |
|---|---|
| The academic table | Every analysis slot is `NULL`. `$coverage` still fills, and `res$meta$note` says why. |
| A proficiency cut for the subject | No red line; `PCT_AT_CUT` is `NA`; `$logistic` is `NULL`, so the landing table has no band and no crossing. `$fairness_logistic` still fits against the English-only average, with `STATE_CUT` `NA`; `ft_check3_fairness()` currently stops with an error in this case, so supply the cut before rendering the report. |
| A scale score on the ELP component the exit rule uses (ELPA21's determination, for example, is level-only) | `$logistic` and `$fairness_logistic` are `NULL`. Box plots and the landing band still work, because bands come from levels. |
| `FRL` on the roster | `$fairness_boxes` is `NULL`. |
| English-only students on the roster | No English-only column; `$fairness_logistic` is `NULL`. |
| A Type 2, 4, 5 or 6 declaration in `policy$exit$types` | `$contested_zone_models` is `NULL`. It is also `NULL` when the zone holds fewer than `min_cell` students. |

## Run it

One call computes every panel:

```{r}
res <- run_check3(bundle, spec)
names(res)
```

On the simulated data this takes a minute or two: it fits two logistic
regressions in each of `r res$meta$panels` panels. Read the sample statement
first. It names the panel the stage report draws:

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(res$meta$sample)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
in_panel <- function(x, subject = res$meta$subject, grade = res$meta$grade) {
  x[x$SUBJECT == subject & x$GRADE == grade, , drop = FALSE]
}
foc     <- in_panel(res$summary_table)
eo      <- foc[foc$GROUP == "English-only", ]
former  <- foc[foc$GROUP == "Former ELs", ]
noband  <- foc[foc$GROUP == "No annual ELP score", ]
bands   <- spec_bands(spec)$labels
top     <- foc[foc$GROUP == bands[[length(bands)]], ]
nexttop <- foc[foc$GROUP == bands[[length(bands) - 1]], ]
lg      <- res$logistic
lg_foc  <- in_panel(lg)
ld      <- res$landing
fl_foc  <- in_panel(res$fairness_logistic)
eo_f    <- in_panel(res$fairness_boxes)
eo_f    <- eo_f[eo_f$GROUP == "English-only", ]
pct     <- function(x) paste0(round(100 * x), "%")
pct1    <- function(x) paste0(format(round(100 * x, 1), nsmall = 1), "%")
cov20   <- res$coverage[res$coverage$GRADE == res$meta$grade &
                          res$coverage$YEAR == 2020L, ]
fp      <- paste("grade", res$meta$grade, res$meta$subject)
box_cap <- paste0(res$meta$subject, " scale score by ELP band, grade ",
                  res$meta$grade, ", ", res$meta$year, ". Grey boxes are ",
                  "reference groups, not bands; the blue 'No annual ELP ",
                  "score' column is not a band either. The diamond is the ",
                  "mean and the dashed red line is the proficiency cut.")
cz_cap  <- paste0("Illustration only. The two predicted curves under a ",
                  "hypothetical composite-plus-floor rule, ", fp, ".")

# The range of ELP scale scores the focal logistic was fitted on (current ELs
# in the panel with an annual ELP score and an academic score). Only the two
# ends are kept; no student row is printed.
ac_f    <- el_academic(bundle)
ac_f    <- ac_f[ac_f$SUBJECT == res$meta$subject &
                  ac_f$GRADE == res$meta$grade &
                  ac_f$YEAR == res$meta$year & !is.na(ac_f$SCALE_SCORE), ]
h_f     <- elp_headline(bundle, spec)
elp_rng <- range(h_f$SCALE_SCORE[paste(h_f$STUDENT_ID, h_f$YEAR) %in%
                                   paste(ac_f$STUDENT_ID, ac_f$YEAR)],
                 na.rm = TRUE)
rm(ac_f, h_f)
cross_txt <- if (is.na(lg_foc$CROSSING)) {
  "is missing, because the fitted curve does not rise"
} else if (lg_foc$CROSSING > elp_rng[2]) {
  paste0("(", round(lg_foc$CROSSING), ") lies above the highest ELP score ",
         "observed among them (", round(elp_rng[2]), "), so ",
         "`CROSSING_IN_RANGE` is `FALSE`: no ELP score seen in this grade ",
         "brings the fitted chance to 50%")
} else if (lg_foc$CROSSING < elp_rng[1]) {
  paste0("(", round(lg_foc$CROSSING), ") lies below the lowest ELP score ",
         "observed among them (", round(elp_rng[1]), "), so ",
         "`CROSSING_IN_RANGE` is `FALSE`")
} else {
  paste0("(", round(lg_foc$CROSSING), ") lies inside the observed ELP ",
         "scores (", round(elp_rng[1]), " to ", round(elp_rng[2]), "), so ",
         "`CROSSING_IN_RANGE` is `TRUE`")
}
n_out   <- sum(!lg$CROSSING_IN_RANGE & !is.na(lg$CROSSING))
st_top  <- res$summary_table[res$summary_table$GROUP == bands[[length(bands)]],
                             c("SUBJECT", "GRADE", "PCT_AT_CUT")]
st_top  <- merge(st_top, ld[, c("SUBJECT", "GRADE", "TOP_BAND_PCT")])
n_top_differs <- sum(abs(st_top$PCT_AT_CUT - st_top$TOP_BAND_PCT) > 1e-9,
                     na.rm = TRUE)
```

### How the panel is chosen

Grade, subject and year are derived, never typed. `compute_panel()` takes the
first subject in the spec's `academic` block, its first declared grade, and
the most recent year the data carry scores for that pairing:

```{r}
str(compute_panel(bundle, spec))
```

`years` lists the years available. 2020 is absent because the simulated data
have no academic scores that year. It is a missing year, not an empty one, so
asking for it returns `NULL` rather than a figure with zero students:

```{r}
gap <- compute_panel(bundle, spec, year = 2020L)
compute_box_data(bundle, spec, gap)
```

### Looking at another grade or subject

Every panel is already in `res`. The figure and table helpers take `subject`
and `grade` selectors:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.8
plot_box_panel(res$box_data, spec, subject = "Math", grade = "8")
```

`run_check3()` also takes `subject`, `grade` and `year`. `subject` limits the
run to one subject, `grade` sets which panel comes first (and so which one the
stage report draws), and `year` applies to every panel:

```{r}
#| eval: false
res_math <- run_check3(bundle, spec, subject = "Math", grade = "8")
```

For one panel alone, pass `compute_panel()` output to a compute function:

```{r}
p <- compute_panel(bundle, spec, subject = "Math", grade = "8")
compute_logistic(bundle, spec, p)[, c("SUBJECT", "GRADE", "YEAR", "N",
                                      "CROSSING", "CROSSING_IN_RANGE")]
```

## What you get

| Slot | What it holds | One row per |
|---|---|---|
| `$box_data` | The five box statistics, the mean and the counts for each group | panel × group |
| `$summary_table` | The same numbers as a table, plus the interquartile range (IQR) | panel × group |
| `$logistic` | The fitted curve and its 50% crossing | panel |
| `$landing` | Where each panel lands, by band and by crossing | panel |
| `$fairness_boxes` | `$box_data` with the English-only group filtered to economically disadvantaged students | panel × group |
| `$fairness_logistic` | The logistic refitted against the English-only average | panel |
| `$contested_zone_models` | The multi-criterion check; `NULL` here | — |
| `$coverage` | Counts by year and grade: who has which scores | year × grade |
| `$meta` | The sample statement, the focal panel, the cut, and two notes | — |

The table slots are keyed by `SUBJECT`, `GRADE` and `YEAR`. None holds student
rows.

### The box plot

```{r}
#| fig-cap: !expr box_cap
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.8
plot_box_panel(res$box_data, spec)
```

Boxes run from the 25th to the 75th percentile, with the median across them;
whiskers reach the minimum and maximum. The figure is drawn from precomputed
statistics, so it always matches the table. A suppressed group keeps its
place as a gap; an empty group is left off.

"No annual ELP score" holds current ELs who were untested that year or took
the alternate ELP form, whose levels are on another scale
(`r noband$N` students here). They keep their own column so the panel loses
no one.

### The summary table

```{r}
ft_check3_summary(res)
```

`N` counts everyone in the group. `N_PLOTTED` ("n scored") counts the scores
the statistics rest on. Students on an alternate academic assessment
(`N_ALTERNATE`) are in `N` but out of the distribution, because their scores
are on another scale. Suppression keys on `N_PLOTTED`. `PCT_AT_CUT` ("At/above
cut") is the share at or above the cut. Three columns sit in the slot but
not in the table:

```{r}
foc[, c("GROUP", "N", "N_PLOTTED", "N_ALTERNATE", "N_WEIGHTED", "SUPPRESSED")]
```

The English-only group's `r eo$N` students are a sample standing for
`r format(eo$N_WEIGHTED, big.mark = ",")` (`N_WEIGHTED`). Use the weighted
figure when you describe its size. `SUPPRESSED` is `TRUE` below `min_cell`.
The statistics are then `NA` and the row stays.

### The logistic regression and its crossing

`compute_logistic()` fits whether each current EL reached the cut against
their ELP scale score. `CROSSING` is the ELP score where the fitted
probability passes 50%: the language level at which a student is as likely
as not to clear the content bar.

```{r}
res$logistic |>
  dplyr::select(SUBJECT, GRADE, N, N_ABOVE, CROSSING, CROSSING_LO,
                CROSSING_HI, CROSSING_IN_RANGE) |>
  head(9)
```

- `N` students were fitted, and `N_ABOVE` of them reached the cut.
- `CROSSING` is `-INTERCEPT / SLOPE`. It is `NA` when the slope is not
  positive, because the curve then never rises through 50%.
- `CROSSING_LO` and `CROSSING_HI` are a 95% interval from the delta method
  (a standard approximation for the uncertainty of a ratio of two
  estimates). It is never trimmed. A wide one means the curve is being read
  past its data.
- `CROSSING_IN_RANGE` is `FALSE` when the crossing lies outside the ELP
  scores observed in the panel. It is then an extrapolation, not a level any
  student was seen at.

In `r fp`, `r pct(lg_foc$N_ABOVE / lg_foc$N)` of the current ELs fitted
reached the cut. The crossing `r cross_txt`. A low share reaching the cut
does not by itself put the crossing out of range; that depends on how the ELP
scores spread. Across all panels, `r n_out` of `r nrow(lg)` crossings are out
of range. `THRESHOLD` and `THRESHOLD_KIND` record the bar used. Here it is
the state's cut.

### Landing statistics

`compute_landing()` reads each panel two ways. `LANDING_BAND` is the first
ELP band in which at least half the students reach the cut (equivalently, the
first band whose median clears it), with `LANDING_PCT` its share.
`LANDING_CROSSING` is the logistic crossing. `EXIT_BAND` is the band the exit
threshold falls in, read from the exit rule, and `LANDING_AT_OR_ABOVE_EXIT`
flags a landing there or higher. `TOP_BAND_PCT` is the largest share at or
above the cut that any band reached, so an empty landing still says how close
the panel came. The table labels it "Highest band's share", but it is not
always the top band's own share: in `r n_top_differs` of `r nrow(ld)` panels
a lower band did better.

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Where each panel lands. A dash means no band reached half. Bold marks a landing at or above the exit band."
ft_check3_landing(res)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Landings read across grades. Triangles mark landings at or above the band the exit threshold falls in."
plot_landing(res$landing, spec)
```

The package writes a summary sentence for this table:

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(check3_landing_note(res))
```

### The fairness checks

Both ask whether the bar set for ELs is one English-speaking peers clear
themselves. Each changes one thing.

**(a) A comparable reference group.** `compute_fairness_boxes()` restricts
the English-only group to economically disadvantaged students, because
comparing ELs with *all* English-only students mixes up language and poverty.
Nothing else changes. The filter counts an `FRL` value of `Y`, `YES`, `1`,
`TRUE` or `T` (any case) as disadvantaged and everything else as not. If your
delivery codes it differently (for example `F` and `R` for free and reduced),
recode it first, or the filtered group comes back empty.

```{r}
ft_check3_summary(res, slot = "fairness_boxes")
```

In `r fp` the English-only row drops from `r eo$N` to `r eo_f$N` sampled
students. Its median moves from `r round(eo$Y_MEDIAN)` to
`r round(eo_f$Y_MEDIAN)` and its share at or above the cut from
`r pct1(eo$PCT_AT_CUT)` to `r pct1(eo_f$PCT_AT_CUT)`.

**(b) A different bar.** `compute_fairness_logistic()` refits the same model
with the outcome "reached the English-only group's average score" (weighted
by `SAMPLE_WEIGHT`) instead of "reached the state's cut".

```{r}
ft_check3_fairness(res)
```

"English-only average" is `THRESHOLD` in `$fairness_logistic` and "State cut"
is `STATE_CUT`. Each crossing column is the ELP score where that curve passes
50%. "Difference" is the state-cut crossing minus the English-only crossing.
A positive difference means the state's cut asks for more English than
reaching the English-only average would. In `r fp` the English-only average
is `r round(fl_foc$THRESHOLD)` against a cut of `r fl_foc$STATE_CUT`.

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(check3_fairness_note(res))
```

### Coverage and the notes in `$meta`

`$coverage` is the data-considerations table: counts by year and grade of who
has which scores.

```{r}
res$coverage |>
  dplyr::filter(GRADE == "3", YEAR >= 2019) |>
  dplyr::select(YEAR, N_CURRENT, N_FORMER, N_NEVER_WEIGHTED,
                N_ACADEMIC_SCORED)
```

It also has `N_CURRENT_ELP` (current ELs with an annual ELP score),
`N_ALTERNATE` (on the alternate ELP form) and `N_NEVER_SAMPLE` (unweighted
English-only). The 2020 row shows the missing year:
`r format(cov20$N_CURRENT, big.mark = ",")` current ELs enrolled in grade 3,
and `N_ACADEMIC_SCORED` is `r cov20$N_ACADEMIC_SCORED`.

`$meta` carries two notes the stage report prints:

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(res$meta$pairing_note)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Reading the band axis

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
cat(res$meta$band_axis_note)
```
:::

## How to read it

**Read three things together:** the landing band, the first band whose
median clears the cut (how much English is enough for this content test, in
this grade and year); how
that compares with the exit threshold, where a gap in either direction is the
finding; and whether the English-only column clears the cut itself.

**Let the reference columns carry the weight.** Former ELs are students the
exit rule has already acted on. The English-only group is the population the
content test was built around. A band's position between them says more than
its position against the cut. In `r fp` the share at or above the cut is
`r pct(former$PCT_AT_CUT)` for former ELs, `r pct(eo$PCT_AT_CUT)` for
English-only students and `r pct(top$PCT_AT_CUT)` in the top band.

**An empty landing is an answer.** When no band reaches half, no observed
level of English is enough on its own to make clearing the content bar more
likely than not. `TOP_BAND_PCT` says how close the best band came.

**Look for agreement across grades and methods.** When the band and the
crossing agree, and neighboring grades land in the same place, the evidence
corroborates itself. Divergence is information too. Read it against Prep 2's
composition findings and Check 1's attrition and selection findings: a grade
with many long-term ELs, or one that lost many students, can land elsewhere
for reasons unrelated to the language threshold. Never settle a divergence by
picking one grade.

**Check where the landings fall.** In the simulated data,
`r sum(!is.na(ld$LANDING_BAND))` of `r nrow(ld)` panels land, and
`r sum(ld$LANDING_AT_OR_ABOVE_EXIT %in% TRUE)` of those land at or above the
exit band, in cells the exit rule is about to empty. A landing there rests on
students the rule is removing, so treat it with the band-axis warning in
mind. In real data, a top band whose median stops rising is a cue to do the
same. (In `r fp` the top band's median is `r round(top$Y_MEDIAN)` against
`r round(nexttop$Y_MEDIAN)` in the band below. The simulated scores depend on
ELP level, not on how close a student is to exiting, so this gap cannot show
selection either way.)

**A fairness gap is a construct-validity signal, not a threshold
recommendation.** An ELP test measures English proficiency, and a content cut
is not automatically a language-access cut. Record the gap for the Decision
stage. Check 3 does not resolve it.

## Pitfalls

- **Never pool grades.** Do not average landings or crossings across grades
  or draw several panels on one axis. Use the selectors.
- **A cross-section is not growth.** A band describes this year's students,
  not a path anyone took.
- **Same year is not same time.** The ELP test
  (`r spec$elp$administration_window` here) comes before the content test, at
  an interval no one controls.
- **2020 is missing, not zero.** Never report it as a year with no
  proficient students.
- **Keep the join direction.** If you rebuild anything, start from the
  academic table, or the reference groups disappear.
- **Report English-only sizes weighted** (`N_WEIGHTED`), or label the sample
  count as a sample.
- **Do not lower the suppression minimum** to make cells appear.
- **Do not read the top bands as the most proficient ELs.** Under the exit
  rule they are mostly students in their final year of status.
- **Do not quote an out-of-range crossing as an ELP level.** When
  `CROSSING_IN_RANGE` is `FALSE`, the number is an extrapolation of the
  fitted curve; report it as lying outside the observed scores, not as a
  score students reach.
- **Use official cuts.** Any cut not from an official table is
  `[DERIVED — VERIFY]` until checked.
- **The filtered English-only group is crude.** One lunch flag narrows the
  comparison; it does not make the groups comparable.
- **Simulated gaps are by construction.** Every EL and English-only gap here
  is a parameter of the generator. Former ELs' advantage over English-only
  students is a fixed shift the generator adds, so nothing here can show that
  exiting causes academic gains. Present simulated output as a demonstration
  of the machinery, never as a finding.

## Decide before moving on

1. **Is the landing stable enough to inform a threshold?** Do the band and the
   crossing agree, and do grades agree? Or does the landing move by grade in
   ways Prep 2 and Check 1 explain? Hold any landing as provisional.
2. **Where do the standard and fairness versions land?** Record the gap
   between the state-cut crossing and the English-only crossing for the
   Decision stage.
3. **Should the English-only comparison be narrowed to economically
   comparable students or taken whole?** If narrowed, which variable in your
   delivery should do it? The package filters on `FRL` only.
4. **Which grades can be read at all?** Check that each has enough students
   after suppression, and that the English-only group is still large enough
   after the economic filter.

Check 4 keeps the current ELs in this cross-section who have both an ELP
level and a content score, and takes its panel from `compute_panel()`, so
the grades you trust here are the ones to read there.

## Additional checks for multi-criterion exit rules

The package names six Types of exit rule: 1 a single overall composite, 2 a
composite plus a floor, 3 a composite plus another source, 4 compensatory,
5 tiered or discretionary, and 6 a domain profile. Check 3's additional check
runs for Types 2, 4, 5 and 6. Check your spec's declaration:

```{r}
spec_exit_types(spec)
spec_has_type(spec, c(2L, 4L, 5L, 6L))
res$contested_zone_models
```

The simulated spec is Type 1. One criterion cannot disagree with itself, so
the slot is `NULL`.

Under a multi-criterion rule, the criteria disagree over a range of ELP
levels, the *contested zone*, which Prep 2 finds. Inside it, Check 3 asks
whether the second criterion does independent work or restates the first.
`compute_contested_models()` returns:

- `$zone`: the range of ELP levels where the criteria disagree, read from
  Prep 2's criteria crosswalk rather than recomputed.
- `$widen`: how far past that range the check looks, in ELP levels (0.5 by
  default). `$n` and `$n_cleared` count the current ELs inside.
- `$boxes`: box statistics by band, split by whether the student cleared the
  other criteria.
- `$model$coefficients` and `$model$curves`: one logistic with the ELP score,
  a cleared-the-other-criteria indicator and their interaction, and the two
  predicted curves it implies.
- `$source`: where the per-criterion outcomes came from.
  `compute_criterion_pass()` derives them from the spec's exit terms, and a
  package test requires them to reproduce Prep 2's own list of students
  blocked by exactly one criterion.

`run_check3()` computes this for the focal panel only. For another grade or
subject, pass a panel: `compute_contested_models(bundle, spec,
compute_panel(bundle, spec, subject = "Math", grade = "8"))`.

To show the shape, this code adds a hypothetical domain floor to the
simulated rule, as the package's tests do. **It is an illustration, not any
state's rule.** For a real state, declare the rule in its spec file.

```{r}
spec_t2 <- spec
spec_t2$policy$exit$types <- 2L
spec_t2$policy$exit$pathways[[1]]$terms <- c(
  spec_t2$policy$exit$pathways[[1]]$terms,
  list(list(component = "listening", measure = "level", op = ">=",
            value = 3.5, exempt_if_absent = FALSE)))
spec_t2 <- validate_el_spec(spec_t2)

cz <- compute_contested_models(bundle, spec_t2)
cz$criteria
cz$boxes[, c("GROUP", "CLEARED", "N", "Y_MEDIAN", "PCT_AT_CUT", "SUPPRESSED")]
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: !expr cz_cap
ggplot2::ggplot(cz$model$curves,
                ggplot2::aes(ELP_SCALE, FITTED, linetype = CLEARED_LABEL)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey60") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "ELP scale score", y = "P(reached the cut)",
                linetype = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Curves that separate mean the second criterion sorts students in a way the
main ELP score does not. Curves that coincide mean it restates the first.
Here the rule is invented and the scores are simulated, so whether these
curves separate says nothing about any real floor.

## Render the stage report

The stage report shows the same results with the stage's own interpretive
text. `render_step()` writes Word and HTML to `reports/` and scans the output
for student identifiers:

```{r}
#| eval: false
render_step("check3")                       # check3_academics.docx and .html
render_step("check3", formats = "html")     # HTML only
```

The example report on the simulated data is
[on the project site](../check3_academics.html).

On its own, `render_step()` builds the stage from the simulated data. For
your delivery, save your results, render from them, and run the disclosure
scan against your own bundle. The report renders in a temporary folder, so
give the spec file as a full path:

```{r}
#| eval: false
res <- run_check3(my_bundle, my_spec)
dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(res, "results/check3_results.rds")   # keep out of the shared folder

files <- render_step("check3",
                     spec_file        = normalizePath("specs/XX_EL_Spec.R"),
                     results_file     = "results/check3_results.rds",
                     check_disclosure = FALSE)
check_output_disclosure(files, my_bundle)
```
